books-all-time.reading: middlemarch quixote season warpeace souls secondsex zhuangzi pedro levi silent solitude republic genji fallingsky iliad redchamber ethicsar analects mobydick proust muqaddimah darwin wretched ulysses critique
books-all-time.gaps: Science, mathematics, economics, religion, art, biography and historical writing remain underrepresented. Bible/Qur’an/other composite scriptures, Euclid, Newton, Marx, Smith and major histories require explicit work-boundary decisions and fuller dossiers. Their absence is not a negative assessment. This comparison cannot yet establish a worldwide Top 25.
tradeoffs: Darwin moves from 3 to 22: this scenario gives direct contemporary reading experience more priority than the historical importance of a scientific argument.
Middlemarch moves from 12 to 1, while Critique of Pure Reason moves from 8 to 25: engagement and preparation change priority without changing the underlying evidence.
The Falling Sky moves from 24 to 14: this is a tentative case for widening intellectual encounter, with particularly incomplete book-level evidence.

literature-all-time.reading: middlemarch quixote season warpeace pedro beloved solitude things earth pride genji lispector godswood kokoro morante cairo solaris redchamber mobydick proust jude sertao doll magic ulysses
literature-all-time.gaps: Major challengers needing deeper comparison include Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina, Dostoevsky, Kafka, Flaubert, Woolf, Borges collections, Manzoni, La Regenta, Indonesian works beyond Pramoedya, South Asian language traditions, Korean and Chinese modern fiction. Existing leads include Godaan, Tamas, Toji, Border Town and Love in a Fallen City. The pool is deliberately provisional; unselected candidates have not been defeated in a global comparison.
tradeoffs: Proust moves from 2 to 20: the recorded disagreement between immersion and abandonment matters much more in the reading scenario.
Ulysses moves from 5 to 25: a first-place Modern Library result remains intact as source evidence, while this draft tests a different reading priority.
Season of Migration to the North moves from 13 to 3. Arabic criticism and rereading testimony help justify investigating this rise; they do not establish a consensus third place.

nonfiction-all-time.title: Nonfiction books, all time
nonfiction-all-time.standing: darwin muqaddimah republic ethicsar critique secondsex souls origins justice spinoza wretched silent liberty blackskin caste enquiry peru levi craft douglass silencing fallingsky injustice worldmaking classics
nonfiction-all-time.reading: souls levi caste silent douglass secondsex liberty blackskin silencing craft fallingsky injustice enquiry republic worldmaking ethicsar origins peru classics justice muqaddimah spinoza wretched darwin critique
nonfiction-all-time.gaps: This first shortlist still overrepresents philosophy and political thought. Expand science, history, economics, travel, memoir, art criticism and biography before calling the list all-subjects representative. Carson and Darwin now have direct supporting material; Levi, Douglass, Bloch and Trouillot need substantially more candidate-specific criticism. Philosophy can qualify as nonfiction, but must not crowd out the rest by default.
tradeoffs: Annihilation of Caste moves from 15 to 3: the recorded comparative praise for argumentative coherence receives greater importance.
On the Origin of Species moves from 1 to 24: a historical scientific landmark need not be the highest-priority book for a reader seeking insight now.
If This Is a Man moves from 18 to 2. That is an editorial hypothesis about testimony, supported by a particularly thin dossier that needs immediate strengthening.

philosophy-books-all-time.reading: enquiry republic zhuangzi liberty caste genealogy secondsex mengzi blackskin analects injustice ethicsar humancondition daodejing meditations bodhi xunzi spinoza justice investigations theological treatise middleway incoherence critique
philosophy-books-all-time.gaps: Avicenna, Aquinas, Śaṅkara, Rāmānuja, Dharmakīrti, Mozi, Mulla Sadra, Kyoto-school works, African philosophy and Latin American philosophy need more work-level comparisons. Further major challengers include Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Hegel, Kierkegaard, Marx, Heidegger, Weil, Murdoch, Parfit and noncanonical women. Verse treatises and collected texts require complete-work and translation checks.
tradeoffs: Hume’s Enquiry moves from 24 to 1; his Treatise moves from 8 to 22. The source explicitly distinguishes the more concise later work from the larger earlier system.
Epistemic Injustice moves from 23 to 11: potential conceptual usefulness rises, while the conflicting reviews remain visible.
Kant moves from 2 to 25 in this scenario. This is a preparation-sensitive reading hypothesis, not a finding of lesser philosophical quality.

philosophers-all-time.reading: hume plato confucius beauvoir nietzsche mill ambedkar arendt fanon mencius aristotle wollstonecraft wiredu spinozap mozi xunzip rawls wittgenstein nagarjuna avicenna shankara ghazali aquinas sadra kant
philosophers-all-time.gaps: This is a reading-engagement ordering of people, not an average of book positions. Socrates needs treatment through mediated texts; Laozi and Zera Yacob need attribution-sensitive handling. Expand Ibn Rushd, al-Farabi, Ramanuja, Tsongkhapa, Dharmakirti, Nishida, Tanabe, Dussel, Oluwole, Oruka, Ramose, Astell, Conway, Sor Juana, Du Bois, and the many European challengers. Absence from the 25-person pilot is not exclusion from the intended 100–200.
tradeoffs: Kant moves from 3 to 25, while Hume moves from 5 to 1: approachable entry works change reading priority, not the historical claim.
Ambedkar moves from 22 to 7, and Beauvoir from 13 to 4: contemporary questions receive more emphasis.
Avicenna moves from 6 to 20: broad historical reception and a suitable first reading encounter are different judgments.
